method: Opened all seven chapter reference targets and inspected the relevant passages. Individual sign captions and artwork reuse the verified register with hash/dimension checks; not a claim that all 76 sign pages were fetched again.

sources.finding: Chapter 2 §§2 and 7 supports authorised directions and railway approach/entry duties. Chapter 3 §§2, 7, 11, 14–15, 21, 23, 30–43 and 51 supports spacing, lane choice, continuous lines, visibility, meeting, overtaking restrictions and exceptions, joining/exiting and unavoidable stops. Chapter 4 §20 confirms vehicle-combination limits; the version effective on the check date is used, not the amendment effective 1 December 2026. Chapter 9 §§1–2 confirms motorway/expressway eligibility and movement restrictions. No legal exception is treated as proof that a manoeuvre is safe.

Supports year-round risk, increased attention around dawn/dusk and periods of animal movement, and caution where wildlife fencing is interrupted. No new collision statistics or species-specific accident duties added.

The advice to other road users explicitly calls for consideration, following distance and overtaking only where appropriate. Supports the lesson without inferring permission from a slow vehicle’s appearance.
Supports the qualitative point that apparent time savings from greater speed can be small. No new numerical time-saving claim is introduced.

The official guide distinguishes a functioning vehicle trapped by barriers (drive through to leave the tracks) from a breakdown (evacuate, move away and call 112). It also says to continue clear when warnings begin during crossing, avoid queues on the tracks and identify the crossing from the back of the crossbuck. The chapter retains the safety qualification on retrieving an ID and invents no ID panel or number.

Supports changed lane arrangements, queues, advance attention, reduced speed, distance and following actual signs/signals/guard instructions. The scene is explicitly partial, not a verified traffic-management layout.
Chapter 3 §§2–3 supports safe traffic performance and critical assessment of personal driving choices. The reflection on impatience follows this purpose.

G6_sources.title: Traffic Regulation (1998:1276)
G6_sources.version: Consolidated live text; relevant current provisions checked 13 October 2026
G6_sources.excerpt: En förare får vända eller backa endast om det kan ske utan fara eller hinder för andra vägtrafikanter.
G6_sources.supports: Turning/leaving road must protect oncoming and same-direction/rear traffic; turning around must avoid danger/obstruction; motorway/expressway turnaround and reversing prohibited.
G6_sources.fallback_reason: Trafikverket example does not specify the complete general legal boundary. Current Swedish statute supplies precise constraints rather than inventing an unconditional route recommendation.
G6_sources.scope_limits: These provisions constrain the conditional editorial example; they do not explicitly recommend return-right routing. Other signs, access restrictions, controls and local rules remain applicable.
